events.text: Let's get practical.
Safety.
What are hosts commonly expected to have?
Start with alarms.
Ontario's fire marshal guidance for short term rentals says working smoke alarms and carbon monoxide alarms should be outside each sleeping area and on every storey.
Local rules may require more, so check with your fire department.
Does Airbnb require them?
Airbnb strongly urges hosts to have smoke and carbon monoxide alarms, test them regularly, and keep the safety devices section of the listing up to date.
If your place only has electric appliances and no attached garage, you can mark that a carbon monoxide alarm isn't needed.
Guests see that section, so keep it accurate.
What should be on a short term rental safety checklist, beyond alarms?
A good model is the self check list the District of Squamish in B C gives its short term rental operators.
Test smoke and carbon monoxide alarms monthly and keep a log.
Replace smoke alarms before they're ten years old.
Have a fire extinguisher mounted and serviced every year.
Keep a level one first aid kit on hand.
And post a fire safety plan near the exits, plus emergency contact information.
Posting emergency information comes up a lot.
It does, and in Toronto it's required.
Since June twenty twenty four, operators there have had to post emergency contact information and exit diagrams in the rental.
Does anyone actually come and check?
In Toronto, yes.
